holidays.name: Make Up Your Own Holiday Day
holidays.description: Today you get to be the founder of a holiday. Pick something you love, give it a name, and invite everyone you know. It could be Dance In Your Socks Day or Second Breakfast Appreciation Day. If you enjoy it, it counts.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has stuck around because it encourages people to invent the celebrations they want.
holidays.funFact: Many of the quirky days on the calendar began the same way, as one person's invention that other people liked enough to repeat.

holidays.name: National Spinach Day
holidays.description: This day honors the leafy green that Popeye made famous. Sauté it, blend it into a smoothie, bake it into a dip, or pile it onto a pizza. Your inner sailor-man will approve.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is a good excuse to eat more greens, and it fits the cartoon sailor's long association with the vegetable.
holidays.funFact: Crystal City, Texas, calls itself the Spinach Capital of the World and has a statue of Popeye in town to honor the vegetable.

holidays.name: Wear a Hat Day
holidays.description: Bring out the fedora, beanie, sombrero, or the silliest topper you own. The day invites you to put something on your head and wear it proudly, whether you're running errands or sitting in a meeting.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a lighthearted excuse to show off your headwear.
holidays.funFact: Hats were once so essential in Western dress that going outdoors bareheaded was considered improper. Today they are mostly a matter of choice, which makes this day a good time to enjoy them.
